brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Provide tidy storage for sewing supplies (compartmentalized organizer)
requirements.evidence: Built 4-cell cluster (piece:0,0,0;full +3 neighbors) with bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments), bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full (full). House rules applied: caps and joint bolts. Compartments allow sorting; dressed with pen, tweezers, tape as small-item stand-ins.

requirements.requirement: Sewing-specific staging (thread, needles, fabric, scissors, bobbins)
requirements.evidence: Configurator has no sewing props (searches for sewing/thread/scissor/needle/bobbin returned 0). Closest workshop props used (tape measure, tweezers, pen). Material-specific sewing supply types cannot be shown.

finish.summary: 4-cell organizer with 9 compartments plus one full bin gives tidy sorting for small sewing supplies. Check_build clear (no issues, meshClash clear). Dressed with generic small props because no sewing props exist in catalog; sewing-specific appearance remains unmet.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
